patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —and form is an accident. The multiplicity and changes of accidents do not entail multiplicity or change in the essence. Moreover, the form belongs not to the essence but to its manifestation in these mirrors: it accrues to what has no essence other than the essence of the one whose form is impressed in these mirrors by facing them. He indicates this as follows.

**Qūnawī:** “That [the mirror exercises influence] is correct in one respect, not absolutely. Influence upon the reflected thing would only be genuine if the mirror changed its reality *as such*—which does not happen. Influence is attributed to the mirror only in the perception of someone who does not know the reality of the thing and has encountered it solely in the mirror. The mirror is not the locus of the reflected thing's reality, but of its image and certain appearances. Appearance is a relation attributed to the thing insofar as its form appears in the mirror; it is not the thing's own reality.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The claim of influence is figuratively legitimate with respect to the image attributed to its original, but false if taken as an unconditional change in the original essence. The mirror affects a likeness, which is attributed to the thing; the reality does not inhere in that likeness, although the likeness figuratively shares the reality’s name. A spectator who has seen the thing only through its reflection may infer that the original has been affected. The analogous spiritual error occurs when someone who witnesses a divine appearance in the mirror of the heart supposes that the reality of the Real has disclosed itself in that heart and imagines that what he sees is the Real. This is an error, not something realized in external reality or knowledge, except insofar as the veiled person’s apprehension is known through eternal or originated knowledge. In that respect it occurs in existence, which is the Real, like other errors.

The mirror never houses the original reality, and this is especially clear where the Real is concerned: His reality is too exalted to be disclosed or directed toward another, as established in the sciences and agreed by the great masters of unveiling. What appears is an image or similitude; likeness does not share the essential constitution of its source, any more than a painted person on a wall possesses the essence of a living, rational human. Moreover no particular image in a heart can encompass divine disclosures, which are inexhaustible.

The mirror thus houses an image representing one appearance. But a difficulty arises: perfected masters speak of reaching the unity of all-unity, subsisting through the Real and witnessing Him. Yet what appeared to their hearts was all they witnessed.

والصورة عرض وكثرة الأعراض وتغيراتها لا يستلزم كثرة الذات وتغيرها ، على أن الصورة ليست للذات بل لظهورها في هذه المرايا عرضت لما لا ذات له سوى ذات من انطبعت الصورة في هذه المرايا بمقابلته وإلى ذلك أشار بما . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وهذا صحيح من وجه ليس مطلقا ، فإن الأثر للمرآة في المنطبع إن كان يصح أن لو أثرت في حقيقته من حيث هو وذلك غير واقع ، وإنما يثبت الأثر للمرآة في المنطبع من حيث إدراك من لا يعرف حقيقة المنطبع ، ولم يدركه إلا في المرآة ، وليست المرآة بمحل لحقيقة المنطبع بل هي مجلي لمثاله وبعض ظهوراته ، والظهور نسبة يضاف إلى المنطبع من حيث انطباع صورته في المرآة ليست عين حقيقة المنطبع ] . 
أي : القول بأن للمرآة أثرا ، وإن كان صحيحا بوجه من الوجوه المجازية لتأثيرها في الصورة التي تضاف إلى المنطبع ، فليس صحيحا مطلقا حتى يكون تأثيره حقيقيّا لا يمكن نفيه ، فإن الأثر للمرآة في المنطبع ، إنما كان يصح على وجه الحقيقة أن لو أثرت المرآة في حقيقة المنطبع وذاته من حيث هي وإنما أثرت في مثله من حيث يضاف إلى المنطبع ، والحقيقة غير حالة في المثال ، وإن شارك المثال ما نبه الحقيقة في الاسم مجازا ولا يثبت في الواقع أثر المرآة في حقيقة المنطبع إلا من حيث إدراك من لم يعرف حقيقة المنطبع ، ولم يدركه إلا في المرآة حتى إنه يتوهم إن حقيقة الحق تجلى في مرآة قلب من تجلى عليه ، فيزعم أنه الحق ، وهو خطأ ليس بواقع في العين والعلم إلا من حيث يعلم إدراك هذا المحجوب بعلم قديم أو حادث ، فيقع في الوجود الذي هو حق من هذا الوجه كسائر الأغلاط . 

ثم أشار إلى بيان وجه الغلط في ذلك بأن المرآة ليس بمحل لحقيقة المنطبع سيما إذا كان المنطبع مثلا الحق تعالى ؛ فإن حقيقته تعالى أجل من أن تجلي أو تتجه لغيره على ما قدر في العلوم وأطبق عليه عظماء الكشف ، بل هي تجل بمثابة ، والمثال لا يشارك الحقيقة كالإنسان المنقوش على الجدار لا يشارك الإنسان الذي هو حيوان ناطق في الحقيقة على أن مثال الحق في القلب لا يطابقه من كل الوجوه ، إذ لا حصر لتجلياته ، بل هو بعض ظهوراته . 

فالمرآة محل لمثاله الذي هو بعض ظهوراته لا غير ، ثم استشعر سؤالا بأن الكمّل قالوا بالوصول إلى أحدية الجمع والبقاء بالحق وشهوده ، وما شهدوا سوى ما في قلوبهم ؛

**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —if it were not His very reality, they could not say this. He answers that this language has a figurative aspect. “The thing has appeared in the mirror” refers to its image or manifestation, not to the essence itself having entered the mirror. Appearance is an attributed relation, not the original reality. An effect on that relation is not an effect on the Essence. We should not say the Real has become restricted by these loci; rather, **His appearances are qualified through them, not His Reality**.

**Qūnawī:** “When I say ‘certain appearances,’ I mean to indicate that there are distinctive essential self-disclosures (*tajalliyāt dhātiyya ikhtiṣāṣiyya*) which occur neither within a locus nor a mirror nor according to a specified rank. Whoever apprehends the Real by these disclosures witnesses the Reality *outside the mirror*, as It is, not according to a locus, rank, particular name, attribute or state, or any such qualification. Such a person knows by taste that the mirror has no effect on the Reality.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The qualified “some” implies disclosures beyond the mirrors of fixed entities, exterior beings and mental forms. These are not merely the Essence appearing to Itself within Itself; prophets and select saints also receive special essential disclosures that do not occur within created loci, fixed entities or a particular rank. Otherwise they would not be purely essential. The objection arises: how can the Essence be disclosed without a rank?

The objection continues: it has already been said that negative absoluteness cannot be apprehended. We answer: what is apprehended here is the Essence without restriction to a rank, although it has descended to ranks. It was not apprehended before descent; otherwise, how could negative absoluteness be ascribed to it? What is intended here, moreover, is before descent to created beings, their entities, and the names connected with them. One who apprehends the Real through these disclosures witnesses the reality of the original—the one whose form can be impressed in a mirror—outside the mirror, as a reality, not as present in a locus or rank.

To forestall the notion of an imaginal appearance still conditioned by a subtle mirror, Qūnawī rules out not only a specified name, attribute or spiritual state, but all such relations and additions. At that moment all are effaced in the Real.

فلو لا أنه عين حقيقته ، لم يمكنهم القول بذلك . 
فأجاب : بأنه نوع من المجاز ؛ لأن الظهور نسبة تضاف إلى المنطبع ، فيقال : ظهر الشيء الفلاني في المرآة ، لا من حيث انطباع حقيقته ، بل من حيث انطباع صورة الظهور وليس عين حقيقة المنطبع ، بل نسبة من نسبة ، فالأثر في الظهور ليس أثرا في حقيقة المنطبع ، فلا يقال : الحق تقيد بهذه المظاهر ، بل ظهوراته تقيدت بها لا حقيقته . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ ومرادي من قولي ببعض ظهوراته التنبيه على أن التجليات الذاتية الاختصاصية لا تكون في مظهر ولا في مرآة ولا بحسب مرتبة ، فإن من أدرك الحق من حيث هذه التجليات ، فقد شهد الحقيقة خارج المرآة من حيث هي لا بحسب مظهر ولا مرتبة كما قلنا ، ولا اسم ولا صفة ولا حال معين ولا غير ذلك ، وهو الذي يعلم ذوقا أن المرآة لا أثر لها في الحقيقة ] . 
وإنما قال : ( بعض ظهوراته ) : تنبيها علي أن للمنطبع الحق ظهورات غير ما في مرايا الأعيان الثابتة والأكوان الخارجية والذهنية ، ولا يختص ذلك بظهور ذاته لذاته وفي ذاته ، بل التجليات الذاتية التي تخص الأنبياء وخواص الأولياء - عليهم الصلاة والسلام - لا يكون في مظهر من الأكوان ولا مرآة من الأعيان ولا بحسب مرتبة معينة ، وإلا لم يكن ذاتية محضة ، لا يقال : كيف يظهر الذات لا بحسب مرتبة . 

وقد سبق أن إطلاق السلبي لا يمكن إدراكه ؛ لأنا نقول : المدرك هذا الذات من غير تقييد بمرتبة ، وإن نزلت إلى المراتب ، وإنما لم يكن إدراكه قبل النزول ، وإلا فكيف يطلق عليه الإطلاق السلبي ، على أن المراد هنا قبل النزول إلى الأكوان وأعيانها والأسماء المتعلقة بها ، ثم ذكر أن من أدرك الحق من هذه التجليات ، فقد شهد حقيقة المنطبع ، أي الذي من شأنه انطباع صورة في المرآة خارج المرآة من حيث هي حقيقة لا بحسب أنها في مظهر ولا بحسب أنها في مرتبته . 

وإنما ذكر ذلك ؛ لئلا يتوهم أنه تخيل ما رآه في المرآة خارج المرآة ، فدفع ذلك الوهم ، ثم بالغ فقال : ولا اسم معين ولا صفة معينة ولا حال معين حتى يقال ، هي من المرايا المعنوية ثم عمم بقوله : ولا غير ذلك ، أي : من النسب والإضافات بمحو الكل في الحقيقي حينئذ .

patches.en:
**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The distinctive essential disclosure outside the mirror shows by taste that the mirror exerts no influence on the Reality. If a mirror were responsible for appearance *as appearance*, every appearance would have to depend upon a mirror; but an appearance without any such mirror is possible. Mirrors therefore condition only some appearances and their accompanying qualities. If they do not alter even appearance considered in itself, still less can they alter the Reality of the one appearing.

**Qūnawī:** “Our master, the Imam—may God sanctify his spirit—used to call these disclosures ‘lightning-like essential disclosures’ (*al-tajalliyāt al-dhātiyya al-barqiyya*). At that time I did not know why he gave them that name or what he meant.” He adds that they occur only for one emptied entirely of every attribute, state and ruling, whether deriving from the necessary order of divine names or the contingent order. This emptiness is absolute, corresponding to the unrestrictedness of the Real. Yet the disclosure does not remain longer than one breath, which is why it is compared to lightning.

Al-Mahāʾimī identifies Qūnawī's master as Muḥyī al-Dīn Ibn ʿArabī, the foremost practitioner of this knowledge. The “lightning” here is not merely the fleeting illumination sometimes experienced at the beginnings of unveiling: those initial flashes are disclosures through divine names, not the distinctive essential disclosure beyond all mirrors. There the Essence is with the names, but the names are not external to the Essence.

**Qūnawī:** “When I heard my master I did not understand the cause or meaning of calling them ‘essential’ and ‘lightning-like’.” The apparent difficulty was that “essential” had been taken as an appearance of the Essence in loci, whereas lightning-like disclosures were associated with the beginnings of the way. Why should the latter qualify the former?

Qūnawī learned the answer when the disclosure was actually granted to him. He repeats both adjectives to prevent the misconception that every divine disclosure requires complete emptiness. Disclosures of the Essence through particular names may demand emptiness from some conditions, not all. These special essential disclosures, by contrast, require complete emptiness from the states, attributes and laws of the necessary named and contingent cosmic orders, for each would serve as a veil blocking disclosure without a locus.

**Qūnawī:** “This emptiness is absolute.” **Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, emptiness of self, heart, spirit, secret, and the more hidden, and of all attributes and states. It does not differ from the absoluteness of the Real—not in the negative sense [the print’s particle is unstable], but in the—

ثم ذكر أن هذا التجلي أي : الذي في غير المرآة ، يعلم ذوقا أن المرآة لا أثر لها في الحقيقة ، إذ لم تؤثر في ظهورها الذي نسب الأثر بسببه إلى المنطبع ؛ وذلك أن لو أثرت في ظهورها من حيث هو ظهور ، لكان كل ظهور متأثر من المرآة ، لكن لما أمكن الظهور بغيرها ، لم يكن متأثرا بها ، بل المتأثر بها بعض الظهورات ، وذلك بحسب أوصاف لا حقه للظهور ، فإذا لم يؤثر في الظهور الذي هو عارض قريب ، لم يؤثر في حقيقته بطريق الأولى . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وكان شيخنا الإمام - قدس اللّه روحه - يسمى هذه التجليات ، التجليات الذاتية البرقية ، وما كنت أعرف يومئذ سبب هذه التسمية ، ولا مراد الشيخ منها ] . 
ثم إن هذه التجليات الذاتية البرقية لا تحصل إلا لذي فراغ تام من سائر الأوصاف والأحوال والأحكام الوجوبية الأسمائية والإمكانية ، وهذا الفراغ مطلق لا يغاير إطلاق الحق ، غير أنه لا مكث له أكثر من نفس واحد ، ولهذا شبه بالبرق . 
وكان الشيخ أمام هذا العلم وأكمل أهله محيي الدين ابن العربي رضي اللّه عنه ، يسمى هذه التجليات التي هي خارج المرآة من غير تقييد بشيء التجليات الذاتية البرقية ، وليست هذه من التجليات البرقية التي يقال : لمبادئ الكشف إذا ظهر انطفأ سريعا ؛ لأنه ليست ذاتية ، بل من الأسمائية ؛ وهناك إن كانت الذات مع الأسماء لكنها ليست خارجية عن الذات . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وما كنت أعرف يوم سماعي من الشيخ سبب تسمية الذاتية البرقية ، ولا مراد الشيخ منها وأهله كان يتوهم بالذاتية ظهور الذات في المظاهر وإن البرقية مخصوصة بالمبادئ ، فكيف يكون في الذاتية ؟ ] . 
ثم لما حصلت له علم وبين سبب حصوله بقوله : ثم إن هذه التجليات الذاتية البرقية أعاد الوصفين ؛ لئلا يتوهم أن كل تجل يحتاج إلى فراغ تام ، بل التجليات الذاتية في المظاهر الأسمائية لا تحتاج إلى الفراغ التام ، بل الفراغ من وجهه ، بخلاف هذه التجليات الاختصاصية ، فإنها لا تحصل إلا لذي فراغ تام من جميع أوصاف الوجود وأحواله والأحكام الوجوبية الأسمائية والإمكانية الكونية ؛ إذ كل واحد منها حجاب لا يمكن معه ظهور الذات بلا مظهر .

... opposed to restriction, not to an actual annihilation of the faculties. “Emptiness” does not mean that self, heart, spirit, secrets, qualities and states cease to exist in reality; it means they are not attended to and do not constitute obstacles. Similarly the Real's unrestrictedness does not mean an absence of attributes, which are eternally and necessarily His. Qūnawī then forestalls the assumption that perfect receptivity would cause this disclosure to continue indefinitely: “It does not remain beyond one breath; therefore it is likened to lightning.” This contrasts with some introductory illuminations which, despite beginning as flashes, may develop into a stable state.

**Qūnawī:** “The reason for its lack of permanence is the ruling of the comprehensive nature of human reality (*jamʿiyyat al-ḥaqīqa al-insāniyya*). Just as this comprehensiveness does not require its continuity, so too, if human comprehensiveness did not contain the emptiness and unrestrictedness that summon these disclosures, it would not comprehensively embrace every attribute and state. Its comprehensive character both establishes this disclosure and negates its permanence.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The author does not spell out explicitly why the disclosure cannot remain for two successive breaths, but it follows from what he says. Human comprehensiveness entails the possession and actualization of diverse states and attributes. When the knower is emptied for this special self-disclosure, those capacities do not cease to exist: they are temporarily unused. If this one mode persisted, the other aspects would remain unactualized; human comprehensiveness would then function as though it were not comprehensive. An objection arises: if the human being is created to be an all-embracing locus, why should an experience that temporarily suspends these capacities ever arise?

Qūnawī's answer is that comprehensiveness prevents the disclosure's indefinite continuation, not its occurrence. If humanity lacked even the possibility of this highest experience, it would fail to include the very greatest possible disclosure and would therefore be incomplete. His formulation underlines the sovereign comprehensiveness of the human constitution: what it does not in any way require cannot belong to its full manifestation. Hence “the judgement of comprehensiveness affirms it and denies its permanence.”

patches.en:
... attributes. Here, although the Essence remains qualified by all of them, it is not veiled by them for a subtle instant, then is veiled by the robe of majesty. The principle that comprehensiveness establishes the disclosure but negates its permanence also implies that the several capacities need not be simultaneously active. Their successive activation is enough, especially given the renewal of creation at every instant. The comprehensive character need not be an actual aggregation of all states in a single instant; the potential for them is significant.

**Qūnawī:** “When God granted me this disclosure I found that it produced extraordinary effects both within me and outwardly. Among them is that, although it does not last for two breaths, it leaves in its locus attributes and knowledges which only God can enumerate.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The passage testifies to the concrete fruits of a disclosure actually received and known through immediate spiritual experience, here treated as stronger than outer sensation and discursive thought for the question at hand. Qūnawī acknowledges the divine gift in the spirit of “Speak of your Lord's blessing” [Q 93:11]. He indicates a subtle point: through spiritual experience it is as though he witnesses it now and it is with him. The extraordinary rulings are those of necessity, extraordinary in relation to the world of origination. These rulings are the lights of the disclosure upon his purified spirit: they remain upon the heart and make it spiritual, upon the soul and make it tranquil and qualified by divine character traits, and upon the body and make it obedient to God’s commands. These are some of the consequences he has in mind when he speaks of unusual effects in his inward and outward constitution.

More particularly, although the disclosure itself does not stay even for two breaths, the heart as its locus retains innumerable divine attributes and unacquired knowledges related to the Essence. During the event their manifestation was so dominant that differentiated attributes did not veil it. When its exceptional dominance ceases, the traces can continue to appear through attributes, which can coexist with the return of ordinary modes. Connection to the highest source of knowledge exceeds what is gained by contact with the intellects or celestial rational souls; the knowledges and attributes thus left behind cannot be enumerated except by the One whose knowledge has no limit. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “On the very night when I wrote this arrival [of knowledge], I came to know that one who has not tasted this witnessing is not a fitting receptacle ...”

الصفات ، وهاهنا وإن كانت الذات متصفة بالجميع ، لكنها لم يحتجب بها ساعة لطيفة ، ثم احتجبت برداء الكبرياء  “ . 
وفهم من قوله :  “ فحكم الجمعية يثبته وينفى دوامه  “ : أن الجمعية لا تقتضي اجتماع الأوصاف والأحوال في آن واحد ؛ بل يكفى حصولها في الإنسان على سبيل التعاقب كيف وهو في كل آن خلق جديد ، ويؤيده إن جعل السبب أثر الجمعية ، هو حصول مقتضاه بالفعل ، والحال إنما هي بالقوة ، فافهم . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ ووجدت لهذا التجلي لما منحنية اللّه أحكاما غريبة في باطني وظاهري ، من جملتها أنه مع عدم مكثه نفسين ، يبقى في المحل من الأوصاف والعلوم ما لا يحصره إلا اللّه ] . 
أشار رضي اللّه عنه إلى فوائد التجلي الحاصلة عند من منحه اللّه تعالى إياه مع الإشعار بأنه استدل عليها بالوجدان الذي هو أقوى من الحس الظاهر والفكر ؛ إظهارا لنعمة اللّه تعالى عليه شكرا عليها وامتثالا لقوله تعالى :وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ[ الضحى : 11 ] وأشار بلطيفة هي أنه بالوجدان الروحي كأنه يشاهده الآن ، وهو معه ، والأحكام الغريبة هي الوجوبية لقرابتها بالنسبة إلى عالم الحدثان ، وتلك الأحكام أنوار التجلي على روحه المطهر بقيت على القلب فجعلته روحانيّا ، والنفس ، فجعلتها مطمئنة مستحقة بالأخلاق الإلهية والجسم فجعلته مطواعا لأوامر اللّه تعالى وغير ذلك . 

ثم بيّن رضي اللّه عنه أن من جملة فوائده أنه مع عدم مكثه نفسين يبقى في محل التجلي ، وهو القلب من الأوصاف الإلهية والعلوم اللّدنيّة اللازمة للذات ، ما لا يحصره إلا اللّه ، وإن غلب ظهورها بحيث لا يحجبها الصفات ، فإذا زال غلبة ظهور الذات مجددة ، بقي ظهورها مع الصفات على المحل ، لأنها تبقى مع الحجاب ، وكان قد اتصل بأعلى معادن العلم ، ومن اتصل بالعقول والنفوس الناطقة السماوية لم يحس حالة من العلوم ، فكيف بمن اتصل بمعدن الكل ، وتلك الصفات والعلوم لما كانت غير متناهية ولا محصورة ، وقد انطبعت في أوسع المجال ، فلا يحصرها إلا من لا حصر له ، وهو اللّه تعالى ، فافهم .

... for inheritance [from prophecy], nor has he understood the secret of the saying ‘I have with God a time in which none but my Lord can contain me’; nor the secret of ‘God was, and nothing was with Him’; nor the secret of God's words ‘Our command is but one, like the blink of an eye’ [Q 54:50]; nor the principiality of existentiation outside any existent time.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Qūnawī reports further, extremely rare effects of this distinctive self-disclosure, learned by him on the night of composition. Someone who has not tasted the lightning-like essential witnessing—who has not apprehended it in direct spiritual experience, indicating that the same reality is not reached by other means—does not, in the strict sense intended here, qualify for the **distinctively prophetic inheritance**. The particular inheritance of the prophets is this supreme self-disclosure; lower grades may also be received by ordinary saints.

The realities of knowledge are not disclosed as they are without this disclosure, since other sources are deficient in comparison. It is therefore not a prophetic inheritance, but an inheritance of saints or philosophers who have connected with the intellects and souls.

Without tasting this witnessing, one does not grasp the inner secret of the report “I have with God a time in which none but my Lord can contain me.” Other disclosures involve attributes or acts, which, when distinguished conceptually, are not the unrestricted Lord in Himself. The taste of this disclosure is required for knowing that secret: one who has not tasted it has not known it through thought, reflection, or sensation, and cannot understand without it the secret that depends upon it, even if he understands its outward wording. [The printed negative particle in this sentence is unstable.]

Similarly the secret of “God was, and nothing was with Him” cannot be fully grasped without this taste. Divine attributes eternally belong to the Essence, so the mind ordinarily cannot envision a state of the Essence without their display. The recipient of a disclosure where attributes are not separately manifested can apprehend that, under the primordial consideration, nothing is “with” Him, just as under that disclosure nothing is “with” Him now. Qūnawī goes on to say that one without this witnessing cannot understand the secret ...

للوراثة ولم يعرف سر قوله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ لي مع اللّه وقت لا يسعني فيه غير ربي  “  “ 1  “ ، ولا سر قوله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ كان اللّه ولا شيء معه  “  “ 2  “ ، ولا سر قوله تعالى :وَما أَمْرُنا إِلَّا واحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍ بِالْبَصَرِ[ القمر : 50 ] ، ولا يعرف مبدئية الإيجاد لا في زمان موجود ] . 
أشار إلى فوائد أخرى عزيزة جدّا لهذا التجلي الاختصاصي ، إن الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه مع جلالة قدره لم يعرفها إلا ليلة كتابة هذا الوارد منها : إن من لم يذق هذا المشهد من التجلي الذاتي البرقي ، أي لم يعرف بالذوق والوجدان قبل ذلك إشعارا بامتناع معرفته بغير ذلك ، لم يكن محلا للورثة النبوية ، فلم يكن من العلماء الذين هم ورثة الأنبياء ، إذ ميراثهم الخاص هذا التجلي لغاية عظمته ، وما دونه كما يكون ميراثهم ، يكون ميراثا لعامة الأولياء أيضا . 

فالميراث الخاص هو هذا التجلي ، على أن حقائق العلوم لا تنكشف كما هي بدون هذا التجلي لنقصان سائر المعادن بالنسبة إليه ، فلا يكون ميراثا نبويّا ، بل ميراث الأولياء أو الحكماء الذين اتصلوا بالعقول والنفوس . 

ومنها : إن من لم يذق هذا المشهد لم يعرف سر قوله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ لي مع اللّه وقت لا يسعني فيه غير ربي  “  “ 3  “ ؛ إذ سائر التجليات إما صفاتية أو أفعالية ، وهي أغيار من حيث مفهوماتها للرب المطلق ولا يشترط لمعرفته ذوق هذا التجلي ، إذ من لم يذق هذا التجلي لم يعرف بفكر ونظر أو حس ، فلا يفهم سر ما يتوقف عليه بدونه ، وإن كان يفهم ظاهره . 
ومنها : أن من لم يذق هذا المشهد ، لم يعرف سر قوله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ كان اللّه ولا شيء معه  “  “ 4  “ ، وذلك أن صفاته تعالى لازمة لذاته ، فلا يتصور الذات بدونها إلا لمن تجلى له الذات من غير ظهوره هذه الصفات ، فيعرفها حينئذ أنه كان في الاعتبار الأول أيضا لا شيء معه ، كما أنه الآن لا شيء معه باعتبار هذا التجلي . 
واشترط أيضا ذوق ذلك لما مر بعينه ، ومنها أن من لم يذق هذا المشهد لم يعرف سر

... of Q 54:50, “Our command is but one”: the divine self-disclosure under this aspect is like a single moment, “like the blink of an eye.” This is characteristic of the special essential disclosure, whereas other forms can continue for two or more instants. Even a reading of the verse as referring to the Last Day can be connected to the same principle, for the general disappearance of things under essential disclosure would be implicated. Without the taste, the matter is not known in the requisite sense.

Another effect is that one who has not tasted this disclosure does not know the principiality of origination without an existent time. Such principiality is essential self-disclosure [the print’s intervening words are defective], because origination, even essential origination, occurs in other considerations and entails a priority and posteriority resembling those within time. He repeats “know” to deny the speculative thinkers’ claim to know this in reality. He begins with inheritance because it is the first rank of this special perfection, then with the absence of any other that can contain him because this is the perfection of the heir; then “nothing with Him,” the perfection of that absence of containment; then the unity of the command. [The printed transition to the principiality of origination is compressed.] Through this the knower descends to the station of subsistence, existing not through himself, for then he would be temporal. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “Likewise one who has tasted this witnessing and has already known that fixed entities are the realities of existents, that they are not produced [as realities], that the Reality of the Real transcends making and being affected, and that there is [no] third matter apart from the Real and the fixed entities, must—if what we have said is properly established for him—know that nothing affects anything else, that things bring about their own effects in themselves, and that what are called efficacious causes and reasons are conditions for the appearance of the effects of things in themselves, not instances of one reality affecting the reality of another.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The purpose is to show that the matters mentioned—becoming an heir, having a heart encompassing his Lord, and knowing the secrets of “nothing with Him,” the unity of the command, and the principiality of origination—depend upon this special essential disclosure as plainly as this question does. One who tastes this witnessing after knowing that the fixed entities, the fixed forms of things in eternal knowledge, are the realities of existents, and that realities are not made, knows that the entities too are not made. These two premises will be explained later. The reality of the Real transcends making and influence, as all sound intellects establish. There is no third matter in the world and in things apart from the Real and the entities: these are confined to existence and realities; existence is the reality of the Real, and realities are the entities. He must therefore—

قوله تعالى : وَما أَمْرُنا إِلَّا واحِدَةٌ [ القمر : 50 ] ، أي : وما شأن تجلينا إلا لحظة واحدة كلمح بالبصر .

وذلك هو التجلي الذاتي الاختصاصي إذ غيره لا ينحصر في ذلك ، إذ قد يبقى زمانين فصاعدا ، ولو حملت الآية على معنى القيامة فكذلك ؛ لأنه عبارة عن فناء الكل بالتجلي الذاتي ، فمن لم يذقه لم يعرفه بالحقيقة .

ومنها : أن من لم يذق هذا التجلي لا يعرف مبدئية الإيجاد لا في زمان موجود ؛ وذلك لأن مبدئية الإيجاد دالّ في زمان هو التجلي الذاتي لوقوع الحدوث ولو بالذات في غيره ، فيقع التقدم والتأخر المشابهان لما في الزمان ، وإنما أعاد لفظة المعرفة نفيا لدعوى النظار بمعرفة ذلك بالحقيقة ، فأكد وإنما ابتدأ يبحث الوارث ؛ لأنها أول مرتبة الكمال الاختصاصي ثم بعدم الواسع ؛ لأنه كمال الوارث ، ثم بلا شيء معه ؛ لأنه كمال عدم الوسع ، ثم بوحدة الأمر ؛ لأنه من جمعه لمبدئية الإيجاد لمشابهته ينزل العارف إلى مقام البقاء ؛ لأنه موجود لا بنفسه حتى يكون زمانيّا ، فافهم .

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ كما أنه من ذاق هذا المشهد ، وقد كان علم أن الأعيان الثابتة هي حقائق الموجودات ، وأنها غير مجعولة وحقيقة الحق منزهة عن الجعل والتأثير ، ومن ثمّ أمر ثالث غير الحق والأعيان ، فإنه يجب أن يعلم إن صح له ما ذكرنا ، أن لا أثر لشيء في شيء ، وأن الأشياء هي المؤثرة في أنفسها ، وإن المسماة عللا وأسبابا مؤثرة ، هي شروط في ظهور آثار الأشياء في أنفسها ، لا أن ثمة حقيقة تؤثر في حقيقة غيرها ] .

الغرض من هذا بيان حال الأمور المذكورة أعني صيرورته وارثا وواسع القلب بربه وعارفا سر  “ ولا شيء معه  “ ، وسر وحدة الأمر ، ومبدئية الإيجاد في توقفها على التجلي الذاتي الاختصاصي ، كتوقف هذه المسألة توقفا ظاهرا ، يعنى : من ذاق هذا المشهد الذي هو التجلي الذاتي الاختصاصي بعد علمه أن الأعيان الثابتة ، 
أي : الصور الثابتة للأشياء في العلم الأزل ، هي حقائق الموجودات والحقائق غير مجعولة ، فالأعيان أيضا غير مجعولة ، والمقدمتان تبينان فيما بعد حقيقة الحق منزهة عن الجعل والتأثير على ما تقرر في العقول السليمة كلها ، وليس في العالم والأشياء أمر ثالث غير الحق والأعيان ؛ لانحصار العالم والأشياء في الوجود والحقائق والوجود حقيقة الحق والحقائق هي الأعيان ، فإنه يجب أن

**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —know, if these premises are established for him, that nothing has an effect upon another thing. An effect would either be imposed upon the fixed entities (which are not made and do not admit essential alteration), upon the Real (which plainly does not admit alteration), or upon their conjunction. But if that conjunction is considered in its existence or its reality, the same problem recurs; if a further composite of those two is proposed, an infinite regress ensues. Nor can an effect alter the reality of the nonexistent qua nonexistent, since under that aspect it has no actual reality to receive an alteration.

The premises concerning nonalterability of the Real and nonproduction of fixed entities explain one aspect. The distinctive self-disclosure provides a further experiential insight: “things affect themselves.” The point is that unrestricted existence embraces all perfections in potential, while the determinate realities of existents are intrinsic affairs whose preparednesses call for the manifestation of their corresponding perfections. In this explanatory register, each determinate reality specifies what is disclosed from the Source in accordance with its capacity; it is this determination of preparedness that is called a thing's influencing itself. He says “if what we have said is established for him” because one may fail to accept the disclosure mentioned and suppose that no disclosure occurs except in a locus. Perfections would then depend upon loci, and the loci would affect existence’s possible perfections. Or one may believe that the entities are made and so affirm an effect upon them.

One might even suppose the divine Reality itself subject to being made and therefore altered by its loci. The objection is that denying causal influence seems sophistical: we plainly encounter causes acting upon one another. Al-Mahāʾimī replies that he does not grant that they are causes: an agent of influence requires a recipient, and once these premises are accepted there is no recipient. The differentiated affairs demand manifestations according to the preparedness of their fixed entities, yet do not independently bring these about. Their manifestations therefore require conditions, as fire latent in a stone appears after another stone strikes it.

Are those conditions then causes of appearance? They are conditions for the occasion and mode of appearing, not causes that create the underlying reality or its essential claim to manifestation. Even concerning appearance they modify its conditions or qualities rather than the bare fact of manifestation. Such conditions include necessary attributes and other things such as intellects, souls, and natures. Calling them causes is not literal. Understand these subtleties, and you will gain the treasures of realities.

يعلم إن صح له ما ذكرنا من هذه المقدمات ، أن لا أثر لشيء في شيء ؛ لأنه إما في الأعيان وليست مجعولة ، وما لا يقبل التأثير بحقيقته ، وأما في الحق وعدم قبوله التأثير ظاهر ، أو في الجمع بينهما ، فأما في وجود الجمع أو في حقيقته ، فيعود الكلام فيه أو المجموع من وجوده وحقيقته ، فيتسلسل ووجود المجموع إن كانت معدومة ، فلا أثر في حقيقة المعدوم ، إذ لا حقيقة له من حيث هو معدوم . 

هذا كله في معرفة أن حقيقة الحق غير قابلة للجعل والتأثير ، وأن الأعيان غير مجعولة ، وأما من التجلي المذكور ، فيعلم أن الأشياء هي المؤثرة في أنفسها ؛ وذلك لأن التجلي المذكور يشهد أن جميع الكمالات حاصلة للوجود المطلق بالقوة ، وهي كامنة فيه ، وأن حقائق الموجودات شؤونه الذاتية المقتضية ظهورها بتلك الكمالات ، وهي الحاكمة على المفيض أن يفيض ما في قوة استعدادها ، فهي المؤثرة في أنفسها ، 

وإنما قال : إن صح له ما ذكرنا إذ يجوز حينئذ أن لا يعتقد التجلي المذكور ، ويزعم ألا تجلي إلا في مظهر ، فيتوقف حصول الكمالات للوجود على المظاهر ، فيكون لها الأثر في كمالاته الممكنة ، ويجوز أن يعتقد كون الأعيان مجعولة ، فيعتقد الأثر فيها . 
ويجوز أن يعتقد أن حقيقة الحق قابلة للجعل ، فيكون للمظاهر تأثير في حقيقة الظاهر ، ثم استشعر سؤالا بأن الكلام سفسطة في ظهور كون بعض الأسباب علة للبعض ، فأجاب بأنا لا نسلم أنها أسباب وعلل ؛ لأن المؤثر لا بد له من قابل ، ولا قابل مع قبول هذه المقدمات ، بل الأشياء لما كانت مؤثرة في نفسها من حيث طلب شؤونها الظهور بكمالات الوجود المطلق ، كل شأن على قدر استعداده في عينه الثابتة ، ولم يستقل بأنفسها توقف الكمالات فيها ، وهي آثارها على شروط توقف ظهور النار من الحجر على ضربة بآخر مثلا . 

لا يقال ، فهي علل الظهور ؛ لأنا نقول : اقتضت الأشياء الظهور ولم تستقل ، فهي شروط للظهور لا علل الثبوت مقتضية ، وهي أعيان الأشياء من قبل ، على أنها لا تؤثر في نفس الظهور بل في صفاته ، فليست مؤثرة أيضا في الشروط الصفات الوجوبية وغيرها من العقول والنفوس والطبائع ، وتسميتها عللا وأسبابا ، ليس على الحقيقة ، فافهم هذه الدقائق تفز بكنوز الحقائق !

patches.en:
**Qūnawī:** “Understand influx (*madad*) in the same way. There is nothing that supplies influx to something other than itself: it reaches from a thing's inward dimension to its outward dimension, and the luminous existential self-disclosure makes this apparent. Making apparent does not affect the underlying reality of what it manifests. Relations affect one another in the sense that some occasions give rise to others, and their ruling appears in the reality that is their origin.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** As you have learned that things’ effects do not come from another but from their inward dimension, understand their existential influx likewise. Their existence is not from another; influx reaches from a thing’s inward dimension to its outward dimension. Although nonexistent externally, it existed in eternal knowledge. That existence was inwardly its own and comes outward through its demand. Its demand does not independently bring it forth, so luminous self-disclosure—the connection of manifest existence—is a condition. This disclosure’s manifestation does not affect the reality of the existence it manifests, since that reality was already obtained inwardly for the fixed entities. Do not object that disclosure, a relation, affects manifestation, another relation, and thus there is real influence. Some relations affect others only in the sense that one causes another to arise in the intellect, so that its ruling appears in the reality that is its source. The ruling becomes an attribute of that reality. Neither the reality as such nor the relation as such is affected; their manifestation presupposes their establishment in their source. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “Among the things known by one who tastes this disclosure is that fixed entities, insofar as they are mirrors, have no effect on the divine existential self-disclosure except through the appearance of the multiplicity [latent] in the unseen of that disclosure. This is an effect on the relation of manifestation belonging to what conditions manifestation. The Real is too exalted to be affected by another; the realities of created things, insofar as they are their own realities, are also above such alteration, since under this aspect in the taste of perfection they are the very affairs of the Real. Nothing other than them can alter them. Thus no mirror *as a mirror* affects the reality reflected in it, for the reasons already explained.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The exact question of the fixed entities' diversification as mirrors of existential self-disclosure is a further point not established by the prior account, which dealt specifically with the alleged effects of mirrors ...

patches.en:
[Continued from the prior page.] The preceding account concerned what happens to the reflected image, the purported efficacy of mirrors upon the effects of things, and the influxes to them. Qūnawī singles out the matter because the contrary opinion is widespread: namely, that the fixed entities, in acting as mirrors for existential self-disclosure, multiply the one existence and make it many, thus exerting an effect upon its multiplication; and that the Real exerts an effect upon these entities by manifesting them after they had remained concealed in nonexistence.

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** One who has witnessed the Real apart from a locus of manifestation knows His perfection to be unrestricted by either unity or plurality. Although unity is the first determination, at that rank it is not simply opposed to plurality: its aspect predominates and plurality remains concealed. The fixed entities do not affect the one existential disclosure by producing plurality in it. Rather, they occasion the manifestation of a multiplicity that was hidden and subordinate within that disclosure. When disclosure is referred to the entities considered under their multiple aspects, the relations of manifestation multiply. It is under this relational consideration that the apparently singular disclosure is described as multiple. Likewise the Real does not alter the entities' very realities through a new plurality. Their relation to the one existential disclosure is a condition for showing the conceptual multiplicity already pertinent to their determination, not a real change impressed upon their essences.

He argues for both assertions. First, if mirrors truly caused a modification of the disclosure, the Real would be acted upon by another. Yet the primordial unitary disclosure pertains to the divine station, whose necessary character precludes being affected by what is other, whether in essence or essential properties. Were there no ground for plurality in the relevant rank, it could not be brought forth simply by the mirrors. Second, if the entities' realities were themselves altered through disclosure, this would amount to a change in the states of the divine Essence, since the entities, before manifestation, are understood as its eternal affairs (*shuʾūn*). Such affairs cannot be affected from without. Through the relation of the unitary disclosure to them, their conceptual multiplicity appears and becomes real. Therefore the mirror, whether identified with the Real or with creation, does not as mirror causally alter the reality of what appears in it. Its role is conditional and relational, not real influence. As explained, influence would be real if a thing affected another’s reality without the addition of a condition. God knows best.

**Qūnawī (continuing onto the next page):** “Understand this text, then, and reflect upon it ...”

patches.en:
**Qūnawī, completing Text Eight:** “For I have placed in it precious sciences and secrets whose worth only God can measure. This is the truth of certainty (*ḥaqq al-yaqīn*) and an unambiguous text. Whatever you hear that differs from it, even if correct, is correct in a relative sense. This is the explicit truth beyond doubt, and God is the one who guides and directs.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Among these precious sciences are the lightning-like essential disclosure; the fact that disclosure in loci does not restrict the One disclosed; His abiding transcendence from contingent events despite His appearance within them; the absence of a causal effect from one intrinsic reality upon another in a fashion that would vitiate unity; the manner in which things' effects are understood in relation to their own realities; the perfection of the human being, its connection with the special disclosure, the latter's cessation, and the benefits that remain. There are also the secrets of prophetic inheritance and capaciousness of the heart, “God was and nothing was with Him,” “Our command is but one” (Q 54:50), and the principiality of origination [without] an existent time.

He calls this “the truth of certainty” because in it the Real does not veil creation, nor creation the Real: the effect of each thing is ascribed to it, yet there is no effect except God’s, and He is not other than them. It is the clarifying definitive text, bringing one to the station of subsistence, with distinction alongside pure divine unity. Formulations that attribute effects to God alone, or alternatively to creatures, are not simply false: action belongs to existence, but becomes manifest through their forms, so each attribution corresponds to one aspect while failing to express the full relation. Apparent difficulties can arise in either direction. This is the explicit truth that excludes doubts. God directs one to the realization of this station, correct without qualification because both revealed law and decree are realized through it, and guides one to understand and follow it through His favour and generosity.

**Text Nine — Qūnawī:** “Among the universal texts are some I recorded in my *Miftāḥ ghayb al-jamʿ wa-tafṣīlih* and in other books I composed, not by adopting the words of anyone else, since that is not my practice. God has safeguarded me against it and through His particular lofty gift made me independent of external, lower borrowings. Yet since this book is devoted to these texts, I must include those texts here also.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having explained disclosure in loci and without them, and the way in which neither locus nor appearance truly alters the other except under a figurative or relative attribution, Qūnawī now turns to another rule ...

patches.en:
[Continued explanation of Text Nine.] The new universal propositions concern the principle that disclosures of the aspect of being a source of many things appear only through loci, and the precise sphere in which their figurative effects can be spoken of. They are universal because each is applicable throughout its particulars, although they develop matters already discussed.

The plural “texts” is appropriate even if there are only two main formulations, since a plural may cover more than one; indeed, the final one contains numerous distinct implications. The reason for repeating earlier formulations is the present work's intention to gather these texts comprehensively. Qūnawī emphasizes that he presents what was originally disclosed to him rather than borrowed from others. Al-Mahāʾimī explains the inferior “external borrowings” as kinds of weakness associated with natural veils in the human descent, which obstruct actualization of intelligible knowledge. He says that his protection from them comes through the special gifts of the disclosures mentioned. “Made me independent” indicates that independence from imitation comes only through these special gifts; otherwise one must imitate the shaykhs. [The print varies between expressions resembling gifts and forms, and has التعليل where the contrast suggests التقليد.]

**Qūnawī:** “Among them I say: everything that is a cause of the existence of multiplicity and of a multitude cannot, precisely insofar as it is such a cause, become determinate through appearance or present itself to a viewer except in something viewed.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Both the abstract “multiplicity” and its many members are specified to signal their real correlation; what counts as one under one aspect, such as the human person, may count as manifold by consideration of all that it comprehends. The qualification “insofar as it is a cause” matters. The intelligible possibility or eternal knowledge of multiplicity needs no external locus. The Real may disclose Himself without any locus; yet His determination *as source of multiplicity* cannot become articulated except in a corresponding object of manifestation. This does not mean that the divine Essence acquires a determination within itself. The detailed display of multiplicity requires mirrors such as the divine names and attributes, intellects, souls, and the remaining levels.

This holds when the Real is spoken of as seeing Himself precisely as the cause of plurality: a determinate vision of actual plurality requires those particular loci. He may know His power to cause plurality without them, but the detailed appearance *qua actual plurality* is conditioned by their presence. Likewise this aspect cannot appear to a creaturely viewer precisely insofar as ...

patches.en:
[Text Nine continued.] The Real cannot display His character as cause of the existence of multiplicity to a servant except through an object of contemplation, because His disclosure without a locus entails the total withdrawal from attention to multiplicity. The two perspectives are thus not conflated.

**Qūnawī:** “Another [universal text] is that no thing produces or brings forth what is contrary to itself or what differs essentially from it, however numerous the classes and kinds of production—intelligible, spiritual, imaginal, imaginative, sensory, and natural. This applies universally to everything called the source of one or more things, or a productive root. But it possesses this description only when considered in respect of what it is in itself, and under another hidden consideration accessible to only a few accomplished investigators.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Nothing proceeds from a thing intentionally, nor does it bear fruit [without] intention, that is its contrary—what stands at the furthest extreme of difference—or is distinct from it in a way preventing either from being predicated of the other. This applies to every genus and form of production: immaterial meanings; spirits and souls; imaginal objects occurring in the separate imaginative domain; bodies and their sensory features; and bodily natural faculties. The rule ranges over special angels appointed to particular tasks, human beings engaged in many activities, and the elements and their generated results, including minerals, plants and animals. A proportion or suitability (*munāsaba*) must subsist between agent and recipient.

But the restriction is decisive: the rule concerns a thing conceived *in respect of itself alone*. With the addition of a further factor, a relation of suitability may arise that was not found in the isolated subject. That is why products fall into such different kinds. Qūnawī also says that there is another, obscure consideration, understood by very few realizers. Al-Mahāʾimī expressly states that he is not one of those who have penetrated it. He conjectures that the additional factor too may require what differs from that opposite or those like things [the printed wording is difficult]. Each thing has a particular Lord, with a manifestation and self-disclosure at a particular time; nothing contrary to its particular object of lordship can come from it. Understand. The suggestion remains explicitly conjectural.

**Qūnawī (continuing):** “Where something appears contrary to what we have set out, that comes about only through some condition or conditions extrinsic to the thing's essence and according to them and the relational configuration arising from their conjunction, namely ...”

**Qūnawī (completing the preceding sentence):** “... the conjunction of the reality described as a source with external conditions and considerations, and the rules of the rank in which that conjunction becomes determined. ‘Each acts according to its own configuration’” (Q 17:84).

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The objection that a contrary or alien result can evidently arise from a thing misses the qualification already stipulated. Such a result is prohibited only when the thing is considered strictly as it is in itself, without further contributing conditions. For example, the universal soul may be described as proceeding from the Real with the first intellect as its condition, or the various lower ranks with a multiplicity of such conditions. Contrary or disparate products arise in virtue of those extrinsic conditions, of the resulting relational configuration, of considerations belonging to essence or conditions, and of the governing properties of the particular rank established by their combination. The source does not require a merely sensory arrangement; a nonmaterial conjunction may also be operative. Hence agency is predicated of the relevant whole, whose several constituent principles each operate according to their specific character. The citation of Q 17:84 functions both as allusion and as support for this account.

**Qūnawī:** “Nor does any thing produce its own identical reality, or anything resembling it in every respect. That would entail that existence had come about twice, appearing within one and the same reality, at one and the same rank, from one and the same aspect, and in one and the same arrangement. This would be obtaining what is already obtained, which is impossible because it has no benefit and amounts to futility; the true, wise and knowing Agent is exalted above a futile act. There must therefore be a difference between roots and what they bring forth.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** He begins what amounts to a third proposition. Just as a thing considered in itself does not produce its own opposite or an alien reality, so it does not produce itself again or something wholly similar in every relevant aspect—reality, level, respect, configuration, time, place and accompanying determinations.

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Qūnawī first says “nor does it bring forth,” suggesting that what does not arise even apart from deliberate intention cannot arise simply through intention, and adds “nor does it appear,” to forestall the supposition that a mirror can reproduce an identical thing or a likeness in absolutely every respect. His assertion that existence would thereby “have come about” is interpreted in the special sense of *appearing*, not as saying that existence itself began in time: the earlier demonstration treated existence as intrinsically necessary. He uses the idiom “obtaining what is already obtained” to capture the impossibility of an exact duplicate manifestation at the same reality, rank, aspect and arrangement.

These conditions must be distinguished. Two different specific realities—a horse and a cow, for example—can share the animal rank, while differing essentially. A reality at one rank can appear under different accidental aspects. An overall arrangement (*nasaq*) is different from any one isolated aspect. Reproducing a thing identical to itself in all these respects would be trivially impossible; producing what resembles it in *every* respect would amount to precisely the same claim, since any real personal difference would already break complete likeness.

The impossibility is explained not as ordinary logical duplication of an already existing acquisition, but as the purposelessness of absolute repetition in divine manifestation. This is impossible for the true Agent, because what is false does not concern Him; the wise Agent, because one who is not wise may act in vain; and the knowing Agent, because another may do so through ignorance. There must therefore be some difference between roots and their fruits. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “The possible things are without limit, whereas the effusion from the Real, the root of all roots, is one. Therefore there is no repetition in existence for anyone who understands what we have said. Understand. Hence the realizers say that the Real, glorified and exalted, has never disclosed Himself twice in one and the same form to one person, nor [in an entirely identical form] to two persons. Some distinction from one aspect or several aspects is inevitable, as I have already indicated. Understand, and God is the guide.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This is another argument against obtaining what is already obtained, understood as manifestation. He makes it clear through two further considerations. First: possible things are without end, as commonly accepted, and each requires a manifestation. If manifestation were repeated, it would exceed the infinite. If each manifestation were set against a possible thing, then, if the possible things did not come to an end before—

**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —manifestations, the lesser would equal the greater. If the possible things came to an end, they would be finite, and manifestations would exceed them by a determinate amount and also come to an end. Thus the infinite, indeed what exceeds it, would be finite. This is the proof by correspondence against an infinite regress.

Second: the effusion from the Real Most High is one, and what is one does not have two appearances in a single mirror. Once these two premises are known and conceded, there is no repetition in existence.

For this reason the realizers, among them Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī and his followers, say that the Real—glorified and exalted—has never disclosed Himself twice in one form to one person. Otherwise the effusion would be multiple, since it would necessarily appear twice in one mirror in one state; but one thing cannot appear multiply in a single mirror in a single state. Nor does He disclose Himself in one form to two persons. Possible things could, as a matter of possibility, be finite, but their infinitude is necessary. Otherwise the second person could repeat the first, and similarly with other possible things; what has not appeared cannot appear in relation to eternal knowledge, so possible things would be finite. This argument is persuasive, as is the practice of the shaykhs. Accordingly, two disclosures must differ in some respect—at least numerically—or in several respects through differences in essential features, accidents, or both together. If repetition among possible things is impossible, its impossibility between the Real and what appears from Him follows all the more. Understand this station, so that you may know that disclosures are infinite and mutually dissimilar, that the Real resembles nothing in which He discloses Himself, and why the shaykhs’ unveilings differ. God guides you to know them.

**Text Ten — Qūnawī:** “Know that, since no attribute or name can be ascribed to the Real under His unrestrictedness, nor any ruling—negative or affirmative—passed upon Him, we understand that attributes, names and judgements are applied or attributed to Him only under determinations. Since it has become clear that every plurality, whether existent or mentally conceived, must be preceded by a unity, the determinations in virtue of which names, attributes and judgements are attributed to the Real must be preceded by a determination that is the principle and source of all determinations. Beyond that is only pure unrestrictedness, which is a negative matter entailing the negation—”

**Qūnawī (completing Text Ten's opening proposition):** “... qualities, judgements, determinations and considerations from the innermost reality of His Essence—exclusion of confinement or enclosure in any attribute, name, determination or anything else we have enumerated or referred to collectively.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** After establishing that roots and fruits cannot be altogether identical, Qūnawī explains differences in their proximity and remoteness according to the fewer or greater mediations involved, and the gifts, recipients and governing rules connected with those mediations. The necessary preliminary is that the Real, when considered under *negative unrestrictedness*, cannot have a predicate, name or ruling ascribed to Him. An attribute is described here as what belongs to an essence, and a name as an essence qualified by an attribute; examples of rulings include life, knowledge and power. Even affirmative and negative judgements of this kind require a determinate respect.

Thus attributes, divine names and their judgements are not predicated of pure unrestrictedness through *ḥaml al-muwāṭaʾa*, nor ascribed through *ḥaml al-ishtiqāq*, except insofar as determinations furnish the appropriate basis.

Because any plurality—whether externally existent or mentally conceived—is understood to presuppose unity, the many determinations presuppose a prior determination that serves as their common principle and source. This determination is called the Principle because there is no distinction there between “principle” and “principle” [the print repeats the word]. He does **not** identify this principle with the absolute Essence under purely negative unrestrictedness. Pure unrestrictedness excludes qualities, determinations and their governing rulings and so is not itself the next determinate source in the explanatory sequence. When determinations are ordered, their corresponding names and attributes are ordered as dependent branches. Qūnawī's stress on nonrestriction forestalls the notion that the Absolute already contains these determinations as a differentiated series without any mediating principle.

**Qūnawī (beginning a new qualification):** “Those of sound intellect, even if they lack veridical unveiling, may consider the order of the attributes and names. If they cannot conceive names or attributes beyond ...”

لما ذكر في النص السابق إنه لا بدّ من اختلاف ما ، بين الأصول والثمرات من وجه أو وجوه مبين هاهنا أن تفاوت الاختلاف ضعفا وشدة من قلة الوسائط وكثرتها ، مع ما يترتب عليهما من العطايا والقابلين لها وأحكامها مع تقديم مقدمة في ذلك يدل على أنه لا بد من واسطة ، وهي أن الحق لما لم يمكن أن ينسب إليه من حيث إطلاقه السلبي صفة ولا اسم ، والصفة ما يقوم بذاته ، والاسم الذات مع الصفة ، أو يحكم عليه بحكم ما ، سلبيّا أو إيجابيا كالحياة والعلم والقدرة . 

اعلم أن الصفات والأسماء والأحكام الناشئة منهما لا تطلق عليه ، أي لا يحمل عليه حمل المواطأة ، ولا ينسب إليه حمل الاشتقاق إلا من حيث التعينات تكون بحسبها الصفات والأسماء والأحكام . 

ثم بيّن رضي اللّه عنه ترتبها ؛ ليستدل بذلك على قلة الوسائط وكثرتها ، فقال : ولما استبان ، أي ظهر بالبديهة والوجدان أن كل كثرة سواء كانت وجودية ، أي موجودة في الخارج أو متعقلة ، أي موجودة في الذهن ، يجب أن تكون مسبوقة بوحدة ، فيكون لكثرة التعينات وحدة تعين سابق عليها ، فلزم أن تكون التعينات التي هي مبادئ إضافة الأسماء والصفات والأحكام إليه ، مسبوقة بتعين هو مبدأ جميع التعينات ومحتدها ، وإن سمي ذلك التعين بالمبدأ لعدم التميز هناك بين المبدأ والمبدأ . 

وإنما قلنا ، هو أصل الجميع ومبدؤها ، بمعنى أنه ليس وراء الإطلاق الصرف ، ولما كان سلبيّا يستلزم سلب الأوصاف وأحكام التعينات ، وما عطف عليه ، فلا يمكن جعله مبدأ لها ، وإذا ترتبت التعينات ترتيب الأسماء والصفات ؛ لأنها فروعها . 

وإنما قال : وعدم التقيد والحصر في وصف أو اسم أو تعين أو غير ذلك لما يتوهم للمحجوبين من أن في الإطلاق تكون هذه الأمور غير مرتبة ، فلا واسطة تكون بين الإطلاق والأشياء . 

قال رضوان اللّه عليه : [ ثم إن لذوي العقول السليمة ، وإن عدموا الكشف الصحيح أن يعتبروا الصفات والأسماء التالية ، فإن تعذر عليهم تعقل أسماء وصفات وراء

**Qūnawī (continued):** “—what they have conceived and their intellectual apprehensions have reached, those names are essential relative to them. Their realities furnish an inference in the phase of theoretical reason, while veiled, because their ruling is comprehensive, the other attributes and names depend upon them, and the determination of what follows depends upon them.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This guides the veiled theologians who deny the ordering of the subsequent names, namely the attributes of acts. Shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī said that these are originated relations ordered after the eternal attributes. If they cannot conceive names and attributes beyond what they have conceived and assert the [eternity] of all of them, even attributes of acts, as the Ḥanafīs do [the print instead reads “nonexistence”], we say: what is prior is the attributes of the Essence relative to attributes of acts. This is inferred from the comprehensive ruling of the essential attributes and the dependence of the others, the attributes of acts, upon them. The determination of the attributes of acts that follow the essential attributes depends upon these in accordance with their realities. Those realities indicate that some are comprehensive and are followed, so the rest depend upon them, whereas others are not. One in the phase of theoretical reason, which is veiling, understands this indication. The qualification is made because those of unveiling do not need it. The clause concerning dependence explains the preceding clause concerning subordination. This dependence and subordination are not temporal: all are eternally beginningless, meaning not preceded by nonexistence. They are ordered through needing what precedes them. This is essential origination, which the theologians do not affirm. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “From this rule one can understand essential and nominal divine gifts. Every gift and good reaching creation from the Real is either an essential gift, a nominal gift, or one combining the Essence and the names.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** He now begins the intended subject. He makes all the gifts divine because they do not relate to the unrestricted Essence. He explains them as goods reaching creation from the Real, excluding pure evil, which, even if it occurred, would not be called a gift. Likewise, what reaches the attributes or fixed entities from the Essence of the Real is not called this, because giving implies prior nonexistence. He first divides gifts into essential and nominal: a gift whose principle is the Essence [without] considering a particular name is essential. We impose this qualification because a mediation is necessary: the Essence as such is independent of—

ما تصورت ، وانتهت إليه إدراكاتهم العقلية ، فتلك الأسماء الذات بالنسبة إليهم ويستدل بحقائقها في طور العقل النظري حال الحجاب ؛ لشمول حكمها وتبعية غيرها من الصفات والأسماء لها وتوقف تعين ما بعدها عليها ]
 . 
إرشاد للمحجوبين من المتكلمين حيث أنكروا ترتب الأسماء التالية وهي صفات الأفعال ، وقد قال الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعري : إنها نسب حادثة مترتبة على الصفات القديمة ، ثم إن تعذر عليهم تعقل أسماء وصفات وراء ما تصوره ، وقالوا بعدم كلها حتى صفات الأفعال كالحنفية . 

فنقول : ما هو المقدم هي صفات الذات بالنسبة إلى صفات الأفعال ، ويستدل على ذلك بشمول حكم صفات الذات للكل وتبعية غيرها من صفات الأفعال . إذ يتوقف تعين ما بعد صفات الذات من صفات الأفعال عليها بحسب مقتضى حقائقها ، فإن حقائقها تدل على أن بعضها متبوعة شاملة ، فيتوقف الباقي عليها وبعضها بخلافه دلالة يفهمها من في طور العقل النظري هو الحجاب . 

وقيد بذلك أفعال الكشف فلا يحتاج إلى ذلك ، وقوله عطف تفسيري ، للتبعية وهذه التبعية والتوقف ليس بالزمان ، فإن جميعها قديمة أزلية بمعنى أنها غير مسبوقة بالعدم ، لكن ترتيبها بحسب احتياجها إلى ما قبلها ، وهو الحدوث الذاتي الذي لا يقول به المتكلمون ، فافهم . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ فالعطايا الإلهية الذاتية والأسمائية يعرف من هذه القاعدة ، بمعنى أن كل عطاء وخير يصل من الحق إلى الخلق ، إما أن يكون عطاء ذاتيّا أو أسمائيّا أو أن يكون مجموعا من الذات والأسماء ]
 . 
شروع في المقصود ، وجعل العطايا كلها إلهية ؛ لأنها لا تتعلق بالذات المطلقة ، وفسرها بالخيرات الواصلة من الحق إلى الخلق ، فاحترز بالخيرات عن الشر المحض ، فإنه على تقدير وقوعه لا يسمى عطاء ، وكذا الواصل من ذات الحق إلى صفاته أو إلى الأعيان الثابتة لا يسمى بذلك ؛ لأن العطاء يشعر بسبق العدم .

**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing Text Ten):** —the worlds. A gift considered in this way is essential, and one considered through a particular name is nominal. A more detailed threefold division turns on the aspect that predominates: where the aspect of necessity prevails, the gift is designated essential; where the aspect of possibility prevails, nominal; where the two are balanced or nearly balanced, a composite gift pertaining jointly to Essence and names. Understand.

**Qūnawī:** “As for essential gifts, no reckoning applies to them, and their determinations cannot be fixed or encompassed by a number. As for nominal gifts and those ascribed jointly to the Essence and the names, either their relation to the Presence of the Essence is stronger and more complete than their relation to the Presence of names and attributes, or the reverse. When the relation to names and attributes predominates, reckoning is applied to them—difficult or easy—according to what predominates and what is subordinated. Here lies a great secret that cannot be divulged. If, however, the result of that predominance is a stronger relation of those gifts to the Presence of the Essence, this is the kind without reckoning, because essential giving and what is more strongly related to it are both issued and received only through an essential correspondence. Nothing else makes such giving necessary.”

**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The rule explains the results attending the respective gifts. Essential giving is not subject to numerical enumeration because it is founded on an essential correspondence between giving and reception; its forms and qualities are not bounded, just as disclosures of the Essence are inexhaustible. Nominal and mixed gifts may incline toward the Essence or toward particular names. If an individuating name governs, the relevant individual instances, duration and conditions have determinate bounds: each name has a specified domain of authority and of what and when it governs. In this register, reckoning may be difficult, involving punishment, or easy, involving reward. He cites Q 84:7–9: whoever receives his record in his right hand “will be called to an easy reckoning” and return joyfully to his people. He says “according to predominance and subordination” to reject the supposition that some names entail—

العالمين ، عطاء ذاتي ، وباعتبار اسم معين عطاء رسمي ، ثم إلى ثلاثة أقسام باعتبار أن ما يغلب فيه جهة الوجوب ، فعطاء ذاتي ، وما يغلب فيه جهة الإمكان ، فعطاء رسمي ، وما فيه الجهتان على التساوي أو قريبا فيه ، فعطاء مجموعي حاصل من مجموع الذات والأسماء ، فافهم " . 

قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ فأما العطايا الذاتية فلا حساب عليها ولا ينضبط تعيناتها بعدد ، ولا ينحصر فيه . وأما العطايا الأسمائية والمنسوبة إلى الذات والأسماء جميعا ، فلا يخلو إما أن تكون نسبتها إلى حضرة الذات أقوى وأتم من نسبتها إلى حضرة الأسماء والصفات ، أو بالعكس ، فإن غلبت نسبتها إلى حضرة الأسماء والصفات أو بالعكس ، فإن غلبت نسبتها إلى الأسماء والصفات على نسبتها إلى الذات ، وقع الحساب عليها إما عسيرا أو يسيرا بحسب الغلبة والمغلوبية الواقعة هناك ، وهنا سر كبير لا يمكن إفشاؤه وإن كانت نتيجة الغلبة والمغلوبية قوة نسبة تلك العطايا إلى حضرة الذات ، فذلك الذي لا حساب عليه ؛ لأن العطاء الذاتي ، وما قويت نسبته إليها لا يصدر ولا يقبل إلا بمناسبة ذاتية ، فلا موجب لها غير تلك المناسبة ] . 

شروع فيما يترتب على هذه العطايا ، فأما العطايا الذاتية بالمعنيين فلا حساب عليها ، لما يأتي أن صدورها وقبولها لمناسبة ذاتية ، ولا ينضبط تعيناتها إلى أنواعها وأوصافها بعدد لا ينحصر من حيث الإفراد فيه : كتجليات الذات لا تتناهى ، وذلك لقوة المناسبة بينهما . 

ثم قال :  “ وأما العطايا الأسمائية  “ ، أي التي غلب فيها جهة الإمكان والمنسوبة إلى الذات والأسماء ، استوت فيها الجهتان أو قريبا من الاستواء : فلا يخلو إما أن تكون نسبتها إلى حضرة الذات بالمعين الأول إلى عدم اعتبار اسم معين أقوى وأتم أولى ، فإن غلب نسبتها إلى الأسماء والصفات باعتبار تعيناتها وقع الحساب عليها باعتبار الأفراد والدوام وعدمها ؛ لأن لسلطنة كل اسم حدا معلوما من المربوبات والأوقات ، وينقسم ذلك الحساب إلى عسير وهو الموجب للعذاب ، ويسير وهو الموجب للثواب . 

قال تعالى :فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ ( 7 ) فَسَوْفَ يُحاسَبُ حِساباً يَسِيراً ( 8 ) وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلى أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُوراً( 9 ) [ الانشقاق : 7 ، 8 ، 9 ] . 

ثم قال : بحسب الغلبة والمغلوبية نفيا لزعم من يتوهم أن بعض الأسماء يقتضي
